items.stem: A manager says 'AI can do anything a human can.' What is the best correction?

options.text: AI is already fully general and needs no oversight
options.rationale: Overstates capability; oversight is still required.

options.text: AI excels at specific tasks but has limits and needs human oversight
options.rationale: Correct: capability is task-specific and bounded.

options.text: AI and human judgement are identical
options.rationale: They differ; AI lacks human judgement and accountability.

items.explanation: Correct: today's AI is strong on specific tasks but has real limits and needs oversight.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO signals suggest a high-value AI use case for a team? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A frequent, time-consuming task that costs the team
options.rationale: Correct: frequency and cost drive value.

options.text: A flashy demo unrelated to the team's work
options.rationale: Novelty without fit is not value.

options.text: Relevant data is available and usable
options.rationale: Correct: data readiness is a feasibility signal.

options.text: No one has asked for it and it solves no problem

items.explanation: Correct: a frequent costly task and available relevant data both signal value.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A team buys an AI tool but usage stays near zero. What is the most likely gap?

options.text: Missing change management, training and workflow fit
options.rationale: Correct: tools alone do not drive adoption.

options.text: The tool is too cheap to be useful
options.rationale: Price does not explain low usage.

options.text: Staff are incapable of learning anything new
options.rationale: Unsupported and dismissive of the real cause.
Many AI tools are adopted when rolled out well.

items.explanation: Correct: adoption needs change management, training and clear workflows, not just a purchase.
